topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the cancer biology lecture series and sets out the learning outcomes for this lecture.

topics.label: Cancer development as a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue organisation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the transformation of normal cells into cancer cells as a process that must be understood within organised tissues rather than through isolated cells alone.

topics.label: Invasion and metastasis in benign and malignant tumours
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how tumour invasion and spread distinguish malignancy from benign growth and how that distinction can be recognised.

topics.label: Colorectal tumour progression and the risks of benign tumours
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics use colorectal precursor lesions to explain progression to malignancy, then qualify that progression by showing that benign tumours neither invariably become malignant nor are necessarily harmless.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour growth and metastatic spread disrupt normal bodily functions and ultimately cause death.

topics.label: Tumour incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the frequency and distribution of tumour types across human populations and animal species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why early cancer detection is difficult and assess how screening can identify treatable disease in different tumour types.

topics.label: Lecture close and upcoming practicals
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the learning outcomes and directs students towards revision and the next teaching sessions.
